docs.title: epyraw
docs.text: Python wrapper for Thermo Fisher RawFileReader library - read .raw mass spectrometry files in Python.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Read Thermo Scientific .raw mass spectrometry files
  • Access spectrum and chromatogram data
  • Extract scan metadata and statistics
  • Support for MS1 and MSn scans
  • Cross-platform (Windows, Linux, macOS)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from epyraw import RawFile, Device

with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1)

    # Get run information
    print(f"Scans: {rf.run_header.spectra_count}")

    # Get a spectrum
    spectrum = rf.get_spectrum(100)
    print(f"Peaks: {spectrum.num_peaks}")

    # Get chromatogram
    tic = rf.get_chromatogram()
    print(f"Time range: {tic.time_range}")

docs.title: Basic Spectrum Analysis
docs.text:
from epyraw import RawFile, Device
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1)

    # Get a spectrum
    spectrum = rf.get_spectrum(100)

    # Plot the spectrum
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    plt.plot(spectrum.masses, spectrum.intensities, 'b-')
    plt.xlabel('m/z')
    plt.ylabel('Intensity')
    plt.title(f'Scan {spectrum.scan_number}')
    plt.show()

docs.title: Total Ion Chromatogram
docs.text:
from epyraw import RawFile, Device, TraceType
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1)

    # Get TIC
    tic = rf.get_chromatogram(TraceType.TIC)

    # Plot
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 5))
    plt.plot(tic.times, tic.intensities, 'g-')
    plt.xlabel('Retention Time (min)')
    plt.ylabel('Total Ion Current')
    plt.title('Total Ion Chromatogram')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

docs.title: Extracting All Spectra
docs.text:
from epyraw import RawFile, Device
import pandas as pd

all_spectra = []

with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1)

    rh = rf.run_header

    for scan_num in range(rh.first_spectrum, rh.last_spectrum + 1):
        spectrum = rf.get_spectrum(scan_num)

        all_spectra.append({
            'scan': scan_num,
            'peaks': spectrum.num_peaks,
            'tic': spectrum.total_ion_current,
            'base_mz': spectrum.base_peak[0],
            'base_intensity': spectrum.base_peak[1]
        })

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(all_spectra)
df.to_csv("spectrum_summary.csv", index=False)

docs.title: Finding Base Peak Across Run
docs.text:
from epyraw import RawFile, Device

with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1)

    rh = rf.run_header
    max_intensity = 0
    base_peak_info = None

    for scan_num in range(rh.first_spectrum, rh.last_spectrum + 1):
        spectrum = rf.get_spectrum(scan_num)

        if spectrum.num_peaks > 0:
            mz, intensity = spectrum.base_peak
            if intensity > max_intensity:
                max_intensity = intensity
                base_peak_info = (scan_num, mz, intensity)

    if base_peak_info:
        scan, mz, intensity = base_peak_info
        print(f"Global base peak:")
        print(f"  Scan: {scan}")
        print(f"  m/z: {mz:.4f}")
        print(f"  Intensity: {intensity:.2e}")

docs.title: MS2 Scan Analysis
docs.text:
from epyraw import RawFile, Device

with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1)

    rh = rf.run_header
    ms2_scans = []

    for scan_num in range(rh.first_spectrum, rh.last_spectrum + 1):
        header = rf.get_scan_header(scan_num)

        if header.ms_level >= 2:
            event = rf.get_scan_event(scan_num)

            for reaction in event.reactions:
                ms2_scans.append({
                    'scan': scan_num,
                    'precursor_mz': reaction.precursor_mass,
                    'collision_energy': reaction.collision_energy
                })

print(f"Found {len(ms2_scans)} MS2 scans")

docs.title: Comparing Multiple Files
docs.text:
from epyraw import RawFile, Device
import pandas as pd

files = ["sample1.raw", "sample2.raw", "sample3.raw"]
results = []

for filepath in files:
    with RawFile(filepath) as rf:
        rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1)

        rh = rf.run_header
        si = rf.sample_information

        results.append({
            'file': filepath,
            'sample': si.sample_name,
            'scans': rh.spectra_count,
            'duration': rh.duration,
            'max_intensity': rh.max_intensity
        })

df = pd.DataFrame(results)
print(df)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or higher
  • pip or uv package manager
  • For Windows: Visual C++ Redistributable (usually pre-installed)

docs.title: Development Installation
docs.text:
For development, clone the repository and install with dev dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/hechth/epyraw.git
cd epyraw

# Using uv
uv sync --dev

# Or using pip
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Verifying Installation
docs.text:
Test that the package is installed correctly:

from epyraw import RawFile, Device

print(f"epyraw version: {RawFile.__module__}")

docs.title: .NET Runtime Issues
docs.text:
If you encounter issues with .NET runtime:

  1. Ensure you have the latest Visual C++ Redistributable on Windows
  2. On Linux, ensure libicu and other dependencies are installed
  3. Try setting the runtime explicitly:
from epyraw import set_runtime
set_runtime("coreclr")  # or "mono"

docs.title: Missing RawFileReader DLLs
docs.text:
The package includes the required .NET assemblies. If you encounter missing DLL errors:

  1. Reinstall the package
  2. Check that antivirus software isn't blocking the DLLs
  3. Verify the DLLs are in the package location: 
    site-packages/epyraw/runtimes/net8old/

docs.title: Getting File Information
docs.text:
with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    # File header
    print(f"Created: {rf.file_header.creation_date}")
    print(f"Operator: {rf.file_header.who_created_id}")

    # Run header
    rh = rf.run_header
    print(f"Scans: {rh.spectra_count}")
    print(f"Duration: {rh.duration:.2f} minutes")
    print(f"Mass range: {rh.low_mass:.2f} - {rh.high_mass:.2f} Da")

    # Sample information
    si = rf.sample_information
    print(f"Sample: {si.sample_name}")

docs.title: Getting a Spectrum
docs.text:
with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1)

    # Get centroid spectrum
    spectrum = rf.get_spectrum(scan_number=100, centroid=True)

    print(f"Scan: {spectrum.scan_number}")
    print(f"Peaks: {spectrum.num_peaks}")
    print(f"Mass range: {spectrum.mass_range}")
    print(f"Base peak: {spectrum.base_peak}")  # (m/z, intensity)
    print(f"TIC: {spectrum.total_ion_current}")

    # Access data arrays
    masses = spectrum.masses      # numpy array
    intensities = spectrum.intensities  # numpy array

docs.title: Converting to DataFrame
docs.text:
import pandas as pd

with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    spectrum = rf.get_spectrum(100)
    df = spectrum.to_pandas()

    # Filter peaks above threshold

docs.title: Getting Chromatograms
docs.text:
from epyraw import TraceType

with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    # Total Ion Chromatogram
    tic = rf.get_chromatogram(trace_type=TraceType.TIC)

    # Base Peak Chromatogram
    bpc = rf.get_chromatogram(trace_type=TraceType.BasePeak)

    print(f"TIC points: {tic.num_points}")
    print(f"Time range: {tic.time_range}")
    print(f"Base peak time: {bpc.base_peak_time:.2f} min")

docs.title: Converting to DataFrame
docs.text:
with RawFile("data.raw") as rf:
    tic = rf.get_chromatogram(TraceType.TIC)
    df = tic.to_pandas()

    # Plot with matplotlib
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    plt.plot(df['time'], df['intensity'])
    plt.xlabel('Retention Time (min)')
    plt.ylabel('Intensity')
    plt.show()

docs.title: RawFile
docs.text:
Wrapper around Thermo RawFileReader's IRawDataPlus interface.

Provides a Pythonic interface to read Thermo Scientific .raw mass spectrometry files.

Example

from epyraw import RawFile, Device with RawFile("data.raw") as rf: ... rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1) ... print(f"Scans: {rf.run_header.spectra_count}") ... spectrum = rf.get_spectrum(100) ... print(f"Peaks: {spectrum.num_peaks}")

docs.title: average_scans(scan_numbers, options=None)
docs.text:
Average an arbitrary list of spectra.

Note: This functionality requires the AverageScans method which may not be available in all library versions. If not available, returns an empty spectrum.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default scan_numbers list[int]

List of scan numbers to average.

required options MassOptions | None

Mass tolerance options. If None, uses defaults.

None

Returns:

Type Description Spectrum

Averaged Spectrum object, or empty spectrum if feature unavailable.

Example

with RawFile("data.raw") as rf: ... rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1) ... scans = [100, 102, 104, 106] ... avg = rf.average_scans(scans)

docs.title: average_scans_in_scan_range(first_scan, last_scan, scan_filter=None, options=None)

First scan number to include.

required last_scan int

Last scan number to include.

required scan_filter ScanFilter | None

Optional scan filter to apply. If None, uses default.

None options MassOptions | None

Mass tolerance options. If None, uses defaults.

None

Returns:

Type Description Spectrum

Averaged Spectrum object, or empty spectrum if feature unavailable.

Example

with RawFile("data.raw") as rf: ... rf.select_instrument(Device.MS, 1) ... avg = rf.average_scans_in_scan_range(100, 110) ... print(f"Averaged {last_scan - first_scan + 1} scans")

docs.title: set_runtime(runtime)
docs.text:
Configure the .NET runtime to use.

This function must be called before opening any RawFile instances. Once a RawFile is opened, changing the runtime has no effect.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default runtime str

The runtime to use. Options are: - "mono": Use Mono runtime (default on Linux/macOS) - "coreclr": Use .NET Core/.NET 5+ runtime - "netfx": Use .NET Framework (Windows only) - "default": Use pythonnet's default runtime detection

required Example

from epyraw import set_runtime, RawFile set_runtime("mono") # or "coreclr" with RawFile("data.raw") as rf: ... pass
